title: Edit Distance
prompt: Given two strings `word1` and `word2`, return the minimum number of operations required to convert `word1` to `word2`. You may insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character, each counting as one operation.

examples.explanation: horse -> rorse (replace h with r) -> rose (delete r) -> ros (delete e).

constraints: word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Think recursively about the last characters of each string: they either match (no operation needed there) or you must insert, delete, or replace to reconcile them.
Define dp[i][j] as the edit distance between word1[0:i] and word2[0:j]. If the last characters match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise you take 1 plus the best of three choices.

The three choices when characters differ correspond exactly to the three operations: replace = dp[i-1][j-1], delete from word1 = dp[i-1][j], insert into word1 = dp[i][j-1]. Take the minimum of the three and add 1.

solution.approach: Classic 2D edit-distance DP. dp[i][j] is the minimum operations to convert word1[0:i] into word2[0:j]. Base cases: converting an empty prefix requires i deletions or j insertions, so dp[i][0] = i and dp[0][j] = j. For each cell, if word1[i-1] == word2[j-1], no operation is needed for these characters, so dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise the best move is 1 plus the minimum of: replace (dp[i-1][j-1]), delete from word1 (dp[i-1][j]), or insert into word1 (dp[i][j-1]) — these three exactly cover every possible last operation that could align the two prefixes. The answer is dp[len(word1)][len(word2)].
